transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Alice Morgan (CTO - Nebula), Ben Chu (Lead ML Engineer - Nebula), Sofia Gomez (DevOps - Nebula), Tom Reed (Product - Nebula)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Jordan from Redwood, and Priya our solutions engineer. Thanks for carving out time. Quick agenda: SDK quickstarts — Python and TypeScript, auth and env setup, and then a short demo of the Console and Optimize features. Then Q&A and POC next steps.

[00:25] Alice: Thanks, Jordan. We're excited. We run most inference on AWS today, some SageMaker endpoints, and a couple of on-prem GPUs for sensitive workloads. Main goals: lower per-token cost, stabilize 95th pct latency, and make rollout/testing easier.

[00:40] Priya: Great, that matches what we've seen with other analytics customers. We'll show a basic Python quickstart, then a TypeScript flow for server-side and edge-ish integration, talk about API keys vs SSO/KMS for credentials, and then how Dedicated or Private deployment could fit.

[01:04] Ben: Quick ask up front — we have strict KMS/HSM requirements for keys on PII workloads. Also need audit logs surfaced to our SIEM.

[01:15] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll cover those. We'll also share SOC2 and ISO artifacts after.

[02:05] Priya: Ok jumping into Python quickstart. (screen share) Minimal code: pip install redwood-sdk, then instantiate client with REDWOOD_API_KEY. Example: "from redwood import RedwoodClient\nclient = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))\nresp = client.generate('Summarize this report...')". Note: with streaming set to true you can get tokens as they emit.

[02:46] Ben: Is the python SDK synchronous or does it support async calls?

[02:50] Priya: There's both. The core client has async methods (await client.generate_async(...)) and sync wrappers. For high throughput we recommend async and connection pooling in your worker processes.

[03:22] Sofia: You mentioned KV cache earlier in the doc — does Redwood support prefix caching to reduce re-tokenization?

[03:28] Priya: Yes, we do prefix/KV cache. It works automatically for repeat prefixes, and you can opt-in to persistent KV cache across requests in Dedicated/Private. (note: sometimes transcriber shows as KV "cash")

[04:10] Jordan: Moving to TypeScript quickstart — we'll show a server-side example and a small Node CLI dev flow.

[04:25] Priya: (screen) npm install @redwoodai/sdk. Example: "import Redwood from '@redwoodai/sdk'\nconst client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });\nconst resp = await client.chat.create({model: 'rwd-3b', messages: [...]})". For browsers we recommend using proxy pattern, not exposing keys client-side.

[05:05] Tom: Are there official TS types / VSCODE snippets?

[05:09] Priya: Yes, the package ships types. I'll share a VScode snippets file in the follow-up.

[06:00] Ben: For auth — we currently use SSO (SAML) for console access and AWS KMS for our secrets. How does Redwood connect to KMS?

[06:12] Jordan: Two patterns: 1) Hosted: Redwood stores API keys (encrypted at rest) and we can integrate with customer KMS for bring-your-own-key in enterprise tiers. 2) Private: your keys never leave your env; you can use HSM/KMS and control key rotation. We'll attach docs. Also audit logs and SIEM forwarding available in Dedicated/Private.

[07:05] Alice: Good. Any latency penalty for KMS integration?

[07:15] Priya: Minimal — auth happens at request setup. For per-token latency we recommend caching short-lived tokens at the application layer and enabling connection re-use.

[08:00] Jordan: Quick demo of Console: route-level dashboards, cost by token, per-model latency percentiles, and a quick Optimize recommendation engine.

[08:20] Priya: (screen) Here's Optimize's suggestions: quantize to int8 for rwd-3b, suggest batching window of 40ms for your 50 req/s profile, and a caching rule for repeated prefix queries used in your analytics pipeline.

[09:10] Ben: If we quantize, how do we monitor quality regressions?

[09:20] Priya: We pair quantization recommendations with eval hooks. You can upload a prompt set and expected outputs; Optimize will run regression checks and alert if quality drops beyond a threshold.

[10:05] Sofia: For the POC, we're planning to test with our nightly batch of 100k prompts. Any tips for setting up benchmarking?

[10:15] Priya: For throughput tests, use our SDK async client with multiple workers, set a realistic token length distribution, and use prefix caching if applicable. We'll provide a benchmark harness you can run in your account or against Redwood dedicated trial.

[11:00] (minor crosstalk)

[11:20] Jordan: Let's go through environment setup checklist quickly: 1) Create a dedicated service account in your IDP for API usage, 2) Store API key in Secrets Manager / KMS, 3) Configure network rules (VPC peering if Dedicated/Private), 4) Add RBAC in Console for roles.

[12:05] Alice: On RBAC — can we limit model versions per team?

[12:12] Priya: Yes, you can pin model versions per route and use RBAC to restrict who can change route configs or rollouts. Canary rollouts supported.

[13:00] Ben: Any terraform or IaC examples for provisioning Redwood resources?

[13:06] Jordan: We have Terraform modules for Dedicated and some example CloudFormation snippets. Priya will share links.

[14:10] Priya: Back to code, quick example for streaming in TS: client.chat.stream({onToken: t => process.stdout.write(t)}) — handles backpressure. For python similar: for token in client.stream_generate(...): yield token.

[15:00] Sofia: We plan to run some parts in GCP and others in AWS — any multi-region considerations?

[15:10] Priya: Redwood supports region-based routing; you can set fallback policies so requests route to nearest region or a cheaper region with graceful degradation.

[16:00] Ben: Pricing — curious about dedicated pricing vs hosted at our scale (100k prompt batch nightly + 50rt/s steady).

[16:15] Jordan: We'll send dedicated pricing sheet; for many customers Dedicated with reserved GPU pools becomes cheaper at sustained throughput. Optimize also reduces token counts via caching/quantization.

[17:05] Tom: How long does a Dedicated rollout usually take?

[17:12] Priya: From contract to live is often 4–8 weeks depending on networking and compliance gating. Private on-prem can take longer.

[18:00] Alice: For the POC we want to run against our test dataset and validate 95th pct latency and cost per unit. Can Redwood run benchmarks in our VPC?

[18:12] Priya: Yes, we can run a connector that pushes workload into your environment or give you a harness to run locally. We'll prepare a harness and an instructions doc.

[19:25] Ben: Any limitations we should be aware of on long-context models?

[19:30] Priya: Depends on model. We support longer context with optimized kernels; for very long contexts we recommend hybrid strategies: chunking + KV cache. There can be memory tradeoffs on a per-GPU basis.

[20:10] Jordan: Quick recap of the code snippets and where we'll host links: Python quickstart, TS quickstart, Docker dev example, and a small CI example to run regression tests on new model versions.

[21:00] Alice: What about compliance evidence? SOC2, ISO, pen test?

[21:06] Jordan: We'll send the SOC2 report, our current ISO status, and pen test summary. For Private deployments we can provide more fine-grained audits.

[22:00] (Priya shares a link in chat: https://redwood.ai/docs/quickstart and a sample repo link)

[22:30] Tom: I'm seeing the quickstart repo — looks good. How do we handle secrets in CI?

[22:40] Priya: Use ephemeral keys for CI runs and store them in your secrets manager; rotate frequently. We support short-lived tokens for automated pipelines.

[23:50] Ben: One technical: how do you handle KV cache invalidation with canary rollouts? If a model variant changes format, do cached prefixes cause bad outputs?

[24:05] Priya: Good question — we tie cache keys to model version. When you rollout a model change you can opt to flush caches or maintain separate cache namespaces to avoid collision. Optimize can also flag risky rollouts.

[24:40] (short pause, typing)

[25:05] Jordan: Let's outline next steps and owners. We'll run a POC: Redwood provides trial API key and benchmark harness; Nebula provides prompt sets and success criteria. We'll target a 1-week POC beginning 2026-12-12.

[25:40] Alice: That works for us tentatively. We'll confirm by Friday.

[26:00] Sofia: Operational question — are there limits on concurrency per API key?

[26:10] Priya: For hosted we do have soft limits and rate limits per plan; these can be raised for Dedicated. For highest throughput we recommend Dedicated with reserved pools.

[27:00] Ben: Can you share a sample docker-compose for running a local dev harness that hits Redwood hosted?

[27:10] Priya: Yes, will include in follow-up. The dockerfile basically sets REDWOOD_API_KEY from env and runs the benchmark script.

[28:00] (brief demo of Optimize charts — latency/cost tradeoff slider)

[29:30] Alice: One last thing — how do you handle PII? If users send PII accidentally, what's retention and deletion?

[29:40] Jordan: Retention policies are configurable; for enterprise we can disable retention and provide strict data deletion policies, and we log access for audits. We'll include the data handling doc.

[31:00] (questions slow down)

[31:20] Ben: About SDKs — how stable is the public API? Breaking changes?

[31:28] Priya: We follow semver and deprecation windows; Console shows deprecation notices, and we support model pinning to avoid surprises.

[33:00] Tom: Anything special about streaming and backpressure for Node?

[33:08] Priya: Node streaming handles backpressure; we expose readable streams, and for web sockets we recommend chunked responses with flow control.

[34:00] Jordan: Ok wrapping up. We'll capture the follow-ups and send the security pack, TS quickstart, and pricing. Also propose POC dates.

[34:20] Alice: Sounds good, thanks.

[34:35] (end of main content — small chatter)

[54:10] Jordan: final quick note — I'll add the sandbox API key to the CRM and send it in a secure email.

[54:30] Priya: I'll drop the sample Dockerfile and TS snippet.

[54:45] Alice: Thanks everyone.

[54:55] Jordan: Thanks all. Bye.
